scenes.title: Home · what Journey Lab is
scenes.speech: Journey Lab helps you understand your product through the eyes of AI personas. Each brings different goals, expectations, and constraints. Follow their journeys, discover what helps or frustrates them, and turn that feedback into better experiences.
scenes.screen: Start on the Home hero. Hold the product definition and central Gather illustration; move the pointer from Alex to Maya. One gentle scroll reaches the four-step workflow.

Scroll to How Journey Lab works near the end of this beat.
scenes.note: The six Home persona curves are illustrative. Only Alex and Maya's recorded case is used as outcome evidence.

scenes.title: Home · how Journey Lab works
scenes.speech: The workflow is simple: define a persona, give it a mission, explore your app, then improve and compare. Meta’s Muse Voice Transcribe turns spoken briefs into editable text. Muse Wonder helps draft the persona and mission, then navigates the working interface. You choose the goals and review the outcome.

scenes.note: Describe available voice input; do not mime recording or show a fabricated transcript. Model execution is not part of this timed beat.

scenes.title: Gather · persona and mission
scenes.speech: Let’s open Gather, our example booking app. Alex wants a quick reservation. Maya must stay within two hundred fifty dollars. Their mission is the same: book a room for twelve, with a projector. These constraints shape their choices. Maya’s budget includes equipment and service fees.
scenes.screen: Show Maya's live persona preview and Personal goal; then the existing Book a room that fits mission. The fixed session pair supplies the actual persona versions.

Show the specific task and success conditions; move to the prepared recorded Maya journey at the next beat.
scenes.note: Do not save edits or launch a fresh mission while presenting. Gather is explicitly introduced as an example app.

scenes.title: Journey · discover the friction
scenes.speech: Here’s Maya’s recorded journey, powered by Muse Wonder. It chooses what to click from the interface, guided by her constraints. She sees two hundred twenty dollars, but the full price is two eighty. Over budget. She changes rooms and loses the meeting name she already entered. She eventually books, but repeats work. A completed booking alone would hide that friction.

scenes.title: Fix · from image to working code
scenes.speech: Now let’s turn those findings into a better experience. Muse Image creates a visual proposal from a captured screen. The design gives the coding agent visual direction. Muse Code, using Muse Spark one point three, implements the selected direction in an isolated candidate. Here are the proposal, the working result, and the actual code changes. Full prices appear earlier, and entered details are preserved.

scenes.title: Retest · verify both perspectives
scenes.speech: Then Muse Wonder retests both personas in fresh sessions. In this comparison, Maya goes from ten actions to five. Alex stays at six, preserving his quick path. Both still reach their original booking goal. The configured checks pass, and the code and recordings remain available for review. Your team decides what to ship.

scenes.note: Action counts are computed from recorded action events in this exact pair. They are not elapsed-time savings, conversion lift, or measured human sentiment. If counters are absent from this screen, use a sourced lower-third in the final edit; the raw capture stays the app.

scenes.title: Close · value and contribution
scenes.speech: Built during this hackathon, Journey Lab helps developers, designers, and product teams investigate changes before release. These simulated journeys give us better questions to validate with real people. Journey Lab. One product. Many journeys.
